issues: Assumption: 'counts over time' means the number of vehicles visible in each frame, plotted over time. That needs only per-frame detection, not identity tracking.
Counting unique vehicles that enter or leave over time would need multi-frame tracking, which the platform does not support. Only per-frame occupancy counts are provided.
Assumption: vehicles are split into car, truck/van, and motorcycle. Buses and bicycles are excluded unless requested.
Pickup trucks and vans may be confused with cars. The car vs truck boundary should be reviewed after auto-labelling.
summary: Detect cars, trucks/vans and motorcycles in a fixed parking-lot camera view so per-frame vehicle counts can be charted over time.

classes.name: car
classes.description: A passenger car (sedan, hatchback, SUV), parked or moving in the lot.

classes.name: truck
classes.description: A larger vehicle such as a pickup truck, van or delivery truck in the lot.

classes.name: motorcycle
classes.description: A motorcycle or scooter, parked or ridden in the lot.

visual_conditions: Daytime with bright sun and hard shadows
Night under artificial lot lighting, including headlight glare
Rain, wet reflective asphalt, and snow-covered vehicles
Densely packed rows where vehicles partially occlude each other
Vehicles far from the camera appearing small
Vehicles in motion as well as parked
Empty or nearly empty lot as well as a full lot
Varied vehicle colours, including dark cars at night
test_scenarios: A separate day's recording at peak occupancy (full lot) with heavy occlusion
A night recording under lot lights on a different day
Early morning with a near-empty lot and long shadows
A second camera angle or position over the same lot, if available
synthetic_targets: Night-time versions of daytime frames with lot lighting and headlight glare
Rain, snow and fog overlays on parked rows
Additional motorcycles and trucks inserted to balance rare classes
Small distant vehicles at the far end of the lot
prompt: Detect vehicles in my parking lot and show their counts over time.
